venue.name: National Toy Museum of Canada
venue.description: The National Toy Museum of Canada is a volunteer run, not for profit museum in downtown Victoria. It is open to visitors at 719 Yates Street, in the back of a space it shares with the vintage toy shop Cherry Bomb Toys, between the Interactivity Board Game Cafe and the Haunted Mini Golf. Displays cover toy lines from different eras and retro gaming consoles from Coleco, Atari, Panasonic and Nintendo, and they change often. The site says the museum is currently expanding its footage to include more displays.
restrictions: Please note there is no touching allowed in the museum and no photos, videos or live-streaming.
venue.hours_notes: Monday to Sunday 11 am to 5 pm. Closed some statutory holidays.

programs.name: Group Visit
programs.description: A self guided walk through the museum displays at the back of the shared space with Cherry Bomb Toys. The published admission is $10 for adults, $7 for seniors, $5 for youth 14 and under, and $25 for a family pass covering two adults and up to four youths. Access 2 cards are accepted. The site says to contact the museum for group rates for school classes, so a class may pay less than the walk in price. Nothing may be touched and photos, video and live streaming are not allowed.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through a small museum at the back of a toy shop and look at cases of toys from different eras, dolls and retro gaming consoles, without handling anything.
programs.our_note: Everything is behind glass and there is no touching at all, which is a lot to ask of under fives in a room full of toys. The entrance is through a working toy shop, so a group walks past the merchandise on the way in and out. Contact them for a class rate before you go, because only the walk in prices are published.
programs.practical_summary: Open every day from 11 am to 5 pm, with children 14 and under at $5 and a class rate available on request. Washrooms, a lunch spot, step free access and how big a group they can take are not stated on the site, so ask before you book.

images.alt: A dark sign reading The National Toy Museum of Canada above an entrance flanked by wooden and glass cabinets full of small figures.
The inside of a toy shop with a Cherry Bomb Toys sign over the counter, glass cases of dolls and shelves of boxed toys.
A row of small arcade machines labelled Frogger and Pac-Man standing behind glass.
Batman, Robin and Spider-Man action figures standing in a display case in front of comic book artwork.

The group rate for school classes is not published. The site says to contact the museum for it, so the price recorded here is the walk in youth price of $5 for 14 and under.
No age or grade range is published for a group visit, and the youngest age they will take is not stated.
How large a group the museum can take at once is not stated. It is described as a small space at the back of a shop.
How long a visit takes is not stated.
How much notice a group booking needs is not stated.
Washrooms, a lunch space, step free access, stroller access and parking are not mentioned anywhere on the site.
How many adults have to come is not stated, and there is no mention of free entry for teachers or chaperones.
The gallery page on the site is labelled as photographs of the previous location, so the two 2016 display photographs used here appear on the current home page but may show the earlier premises.
